experiment.steer: S015 §8 (PTX is a named C2M input)

corpus.why_this_corpus: the steer says to use the seed as a PTX corpus; this is PTX the project itself ships, not PTX I wrote to suit my own parser

higher_tiers.C2M-T1: NOT CLAIMED: no runtime, memory API or stream semantics exist
higher_tiers.C2M-T2: NOT CLAIMED: no math/ML kernel corpus (no GEMM, no reduction)
higher_tiers.C2M-T3: NOT CLAIMED: no real open CUDA project has been run

conformance.why_not: no NVIDIA hardware is present, so nothing was compared against CUDA itself; P2 remains open

an_increment_that_bought_nothing.hypothesis: cvta.to.global.u64 blocked 43 of 291 files -- the single most common refusal -- so supporting it should raise coverage substantially
an_increment_that_bought_nothing.action: added cvta as a pointer-identity passthrough, plus mad.lo.u32, mul.wide.u32/s32 and cvt.s64.s32 index arithmetic
an_increment_that_bought_nothing.result: coverage UNCHANGED at 3/291. The blocker simply MOVED to ld.global.u32 on the same 43 files.
an_increment_that_bought_nothing.what_it_means: those files need integer loads AND more besides, so they were never one instruction away. Adding the most-frequent refusal reason is NOT the same as adding the binding constraint, and a refusal histogram ranks SYMPTOMS rather than causes. The honest read is that this subset is far from the corpus, not one step from it.

claim_boundary: C2M translates 3 of the 291 PTX files the pinned seed ships -- ONE PERCENT -- and all 3 execute on the Apple GPU and match a numpy oracle. That is the whole claim. It is still C2M-T0: no runtime, no memory API, no streams, so T1 through T5 remain NOT CLAIMED. The oracle is numpy on CPU, NOT CUDA, so this is still not a differential and P2 stays open. And 288 files are refused, each with the instruction named.
